abstract: This work systematically articulates the Yin-Yang homeodynamics coordination between Nrf1 and Nrf2, resolving the longstanding core paradox in redox biology of why robust Nrf2-mediated antioxidant activation frequently fails to fully eliminate unresolved oxidative stress and re-establish sustained redox homeostasis. Integrating multi-omic expression profiles from human HepG2 cells and primary murine hepatocytes, we constructed an 11-variable endogenous regulatory network model, demonstrating that Nrf2 exclusively mediates transient acute stress attenuation responses, while Nrf1 functions as the non-redundant upstream organiser that supplies the indispensable preconditions for definitive stress resolution via three irreplaceable homeostatic axes: organelle integrity maintenance, proteasome functional recovery, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) cholesterol steady-state handling. Their coupled regulatory interactions generate a bistable configuration demarcated by an index-1 saddle point, partitioning the physiological state space into native low-stress homeostasis and the previously uncharacterised persistent-stress attractor. Once self-amplified unresolved endogenous stress generation reaches dynamic flux balance with Nrf2-dependent clearance at an elevated burden level, the system becomes irreversibly locked in this persistent high-burden equilibrium, and cannot spontaneously return to native homeostatic status even after the initiating upstream disturbance has been fully corrected. Collectively, this study fundamentally delineates the clear functional division between transient antioxidant activation and durable redox recovery during Nrf1/Nrf2 homeodynamics, hence providing a rigorous systems-level theoretical framework to guide future translational interventions targeting redox homeostasis restoration.
